title: Backstage 1.55 Adds Scaffolder Task Recovery and Removes Deprecated Catalog APIs
gist: Backstage 1.55 adds opt-in scaffolder task recovery that resumes crashed or timed-out tasks, but also removes deprecated catalog APIs and requires Elasticsearch 8.19+, giving platform teams several breaking changes. It also includes GitLab action performance gains and security fixes in seven packages.

insights.claim: Backstage 1.55 adds scaffolder.taskRecovery, which resumes a crashed or timed-out Software Template task from its last completed step, retains secrets until terminal state and persists step outputs, replacing three experimental flags.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Reduces failures in internal developer portal automation, improving platform reliability.
insights.locator: Task recovery sits behind a new

insights.claim: Because a resumed task can run an action twice, release notes warn that actions in recovered tasks should be idempotent or use checkpoints.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Platform teams must audit custom actions before enabling recovery.
insights.locator: The release notes warn that actions

insights.claim: Workspace serialization needs a separate provider; the new database provider has a 50 MB limit and is for development only, with production pointed to the GCP module or a similar external store.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Production use implies extra storage setup and cloud dependency.

insights.claim: The feature answers a long-standing request, such as a 2025 GitHub issue where re-running the whole scaffolder process was called inconvenient and technically problematic, though it covers only crashes and time-outs.
insights.speaker: Manoj Azad (quoted by Mark Silvester)
insights.locator: The feature responds to a long-standing request

insights.claim: 1.55 drops catalog.enableRelationsCompatibility so relations return only targetRef, removes CodeOwnersProcessor and AnnotateScmSlugEntityProcessor in favor of community modules, and requires Elasticsearch 8.19 or later (AWS and OpenSearch providers unaffected).
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Adopters face migration work; the shift of features to community modules signals maintenance triage.
insights.locator: Most of the upgrade work sits in the breaking changes

insights.claim: TechDocs now strips MkDocs plugins not on a built-in allowlist, and teams needing others must list them under techdocs.generator.mkdocs.dangerouslyAllowAdditionalPlugins.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Security hardening comes at the cost of flexibility.

insights.claim: Permission policies that deny unknown permissions must now explicitly allow scaffolder.template.dry-run, and scaffolder.requireScmUserCredentials requires user-provided credentials for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps actions.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Governance tightening moves portals away from shared service credentials.
insights.locator: Several changes target governance and speed

insights.claim: A Veepee SRE changed GitLab merge-request and push actions to compare files locally, cutting API requests for a repo of a few hundred files from about 300 to under ten and a step from 5-15 seconds to about 3 seconds.
insights.speaker: Michael Todorovic
insights.so_what: Shows large efficiency gains from removing redundant API calls in self-hosted setups.
insights.quote: It turned out almost all of that was the action asking GitLab for information it already had.
insights.locator: Several changes target governance and speed

insights.claim: Core plugins (catalog, search, TechDocs) now lazy-load pages to shrink the initial bundle, and the release lists security fixes in seven packages, including OIDC, Cloudflare Access and the proxy backend.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Security patches in auth providers make timely upgrades necessary.
insights.locator: The release also lists security fixes

insights.claim: Three patch releases (1.55.1-1.55.3) followed within weeks, fixing the new verify-patches command and TechDocs MkDocs extension handling, and 1.56.0-next.2 is already in pre-release.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Rapid patching suggests post-release instability to account for in upgrade planning.
